title: Recording risks, hazard reports and breaches
audience: Cleaning and support workers who record hazards, risks and breaches of infection control in healthcare and care settings.
learningOutcomes: Complete a risk record with the activity, hazard, rating, control measures and timeframe.
Write a hazard report that includes type, location, risk, who is at risk and action taken.
Name the first person to tell about a breach and the other people a report may need to reach.

instruction.heading: Writing a risk record
instruction.body: Begin by naming the activity and the hazards in it. Decide who is at risk and how likely and how serious the harm could be. List the control measures already in place and any new control you recommend, and set a timeframe for each. The guide lays out five columns: what the worker is doing, the danger involved, how serious the danger rates, the measures in place, and when each measure is due. For example, showering a client who has dementia brings risks of a wet floor, aggression or resistance, and falls. Controls include a shower chair and grab rails, and each has a timeframe. Keep the record in the form your employer uses.

instruction.heading: Hazard reports
instruction.body: Spotting a hazard at work means you are obliged to report it. The guide treats this as a legal duty. Write up a hazard report, then hand it to the supervisor or the WHS representative. A hazard report should give the type of hazard, its location, the risk it poses, who is at risk and the action taken. For urgent hazards, speak to the supervisor first and then complete the written report.

instruction.heading: Breaches of infection control
instruction.body: Infection control policies are written to keep everyone safe. The employer must create, explain and train workers in those policies, and workers must learn and follow them. Examples of breaches named in the guide include skipping hand cleaning at the required moments, putting protective items on or taking them off incorrectly, attending while unwell, reusing a needle meant for one use, reusing equipment that has not been reprocessed, weak respiratory etiquette, and disregarding signs. A breach is reported to the supervisor, not corrected publicly. Agency staff may not know the local policy, so a reminder and the correct protocol are often the right first step, before any formal document is written.

instruction.heading: Who receives which report
instruction.body: Go to the supervisor first, speaking directly and without delay, and bring one or two possible fixes so the supervisor can accept one or suggest a different option. Other people may need a report depending on the situation: a registered nurse, a general practitioner, other health professionals, a carer, a family member or guardian, and the regulating bodies. The regulator, which the guide calls the responsible authority, creates and enforces the rules, and investigates when there are repeated breaches. Share information only with people who need it, and keep records in the designated clean administration area (see “Clean zones, contaminated zones and signage”).

procedure: Describe the activity and the hazard in plain words.
Decide who is at risk and estimate how likely and how serious the harm could be.
Record the controls already in place and any new control, with a timeframe.
For an urgent hazard or breach, tell the supervisor verbally straight away.
Complete the written hazard report or incident record with the required details, including date, time, names and witnesses.
Store the record in the clean administration area and keep the information private to those who need it.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner finds a cracked lid on a mop bucket in a dental treatment room.
workedExamples.reasoning: A hazard report stating the type of hazard (cracked lid), its location, the risk (contamination and a slip risk), who is at risk, and the action taken (removed from use and reported). A risk record can also show the control and a timeframe for replacement.

workedExamples.situation: A cleaner sees a colleague reuse a single-use needle during a task.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Who is told first, and how is it recorded?
workedExamples.reasoning: Tell the supervisor straight away, verbally. It is a breach of infection control. Record the time, the people involved and any witnesses, and do not confront the colleague publicly.

equipmentAndPpe: Risk record form or the workplace system
Hazard report form and a copy kept by the worker
Secure clean administration area for storing records

commonErrors.error: Holding a report back for a week.
commonErrors.prevention: Report at once and follow up in writing afterwards.

commonErrors.error: Writing a report with names in a shared public space.
commonErrors.prevention: Keep records in the clean administration area and limit who sees them.

commonErrors.error: Telling family or a client before the supervisor.
commonErrors.prevention: Tell the supervisor first, unless the situation is an emergency, and let the supervisor decide the next contact.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Check the duty to report hazards and the reporting rules under work health and safety law for your state or territory. This lesson does not state the rule for any one state.
Share health information only with people who need it, and keep it private from others.
Completing this lesson does not grant a licence, certificate or authority to perform regulated work.

qualityStandard: Learner completes a risk record with all five columns filled in.
Learner writes a hazard report with each of the five required details.
Learner names the supervisor as the first person to tell about a breach.
documentationEvidence: Risk record with activity, hazard, rating, controls and timeframe.
Hazard report or incident record with date, time, names and witnesses.
summary: A risk record names the activity, hazard, rating, controls and timeframe.
Hazards and breaches are reported to the supervisor first, verbally and at once.
Records stay in the clean administration space and reach only the people who need them.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which element belongs in a risk record?
options: The colour of the mop handle
The name of the cleaner pet
The price of the product only

knowledgeChecks.question: A worker sees a colleague reuse a single-use needle. Who should be told first?
options: The client family and their friends
A friend in another ward at lunch time
Nobody, unless it happens again today

knowledgeChecks.question: Which body creates and enforces infection control rules and investigates repeated breaches?
options: A regulator, known in the guide as the responsible authority
The cleaning contractor sales team and its marketing staff
The product manufacturer's sales team, through its own customer rules
Visitors to the facility and the families of the patients
